ISSUE FOUND (blocker for polish, not for launch): duplicate 'Other' profession pill in /professional/verification Step 1 — /api/config already includes 'Other' in professions dict, and verification.tsx:303 unconditionally appends another 'Other' → two identical pills render + React key warning fires on every mount.

ui_bugs.issue: Duplicate 'Other' pill renders. /api/config['professions'] already contains an 'Other' key, but /app/frontend/app/professional/verification.tsx:303 does `[...Object.keys(professions), 'Other']` which appends a second 'Other'. Visible in screenshots (two Other chips at the bottom of the Step 1 grid) and produces the React console error 'Encountered two children with the same key' on every mount. Fix: drop the trailing 'Other' from the spread (Object.keys already includes it), or de-dupe with `Array.from(new Set([...Object.keys(professions), 'Other']))`.

critical_code_review_comments: Backend /api/professional/profile/me correctly auto-creates a professional_profiles doc for Approved verifications and is idempotent (no duplicates on repeated GETs).
Backend /api/pings/{id}/accept enforces range server-side (returns 409 'This person is outside your current range') so the UI 'in_range' flag is not the sole gate — good defence in depth.
Backend /api/professional/profile/{id} public view does not include document base64 payloads (verified by string-scan of the JSON body).
Backend /api/verification/extract gracefully returns 200 with empty fields for tiny images / non-image types — never 500s.

Frontend /(auth)/profile-setup enforces both min-2 photos AND (per spec) the display_name field, but when both are blank only the photo error surfaces (the display_name check is not reached first). Minor UX ordering; not a blocker because the display_name field defaults to `user.name` on first mount, so real users rarely see this.

rca_of_issue: Duplicate 'Other' pill root cause: /api/config already returns 'Other' inside the professions dict (backend server.py). verification.tsx line 303 renders `pills([...Object.keys(professions), 'Other'], ...)` — the trailing 'Other' is redundant. Because both instances share the same testID/key, React logs the key-collision warning and Playwright's query_selector_all returns 2 matches. Reproduction: any user opens /professional/verification. Mitigation: change to `pills(Array.from(new Set([...Object.keys(professions), 'Other'])), ...)` OR simply `pills(Object.keys(professions), ...)` since backend already includes it. One-line fix, no state migration.
